plan.rationale: Frozen objective is latency_ms of one complete batch=32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward on a single GPU (request.json), so the open diagnostic question after the already-run torch collector is whether per-call latency is host-dispatch-bound or GPU-execution-bound. The torch baseline already gives complete kernel attribution (coverage.json: 88 cuda_kernels, 88 associated, 0 unassociated, 0 root_only, 0 ambiguous forward sequences), so nsys is not needed: no overlap, graph-tracing or attribution question remains open. execution_timeline is selected for its CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization points and per-device intervals, which distinguish host submission stalls/launch gaps from GPU execution in the measured invocation; its clock alignment bounds cover CPU submissions only, so GPU readiness stays unknown where unobserved. python_runtime is selected for a warmed cProfile view of host dispatch and binding costs per forward call, used strictly diagnostically since it perturbs execution and its inclusive/self times are not clean performance scores or GPU durations. nccl_tuning, collective_calibration and cross-rank fields are not applicable (single device, no collectives); device_telemetry is skipped because its device-wide NVML utilization/PCIe/memory windows cannot be attributed to the millisecond-scale measured invocation, host-to-device input transfer is excluded from the measured unit, and peak_allocated_bytes is already available from torch; binding_cost and candidate diagnostics are skipped because no candidate exists yet.
